$comment: Copy to .claude/config/lint-gate.json in your project. All three keys are optional;
an absent key means that check never runs. There are no defaults — a command is only
run if the project asked for it by name.
format   runs after every Edit/Write, on that one file. Use {file} to place the path,
otherwise it is appended. The path is shell-quoted for you.
lint     runs on Stop and TeammateIdle, never per-edit.
typecheck runs on Stop and TeammateIdle, after lint.
Formatting is per-edit because it is a syntactic transform that is valid on any file
that parses. Linting and typechecking are not: an import added in one edit and used in
the next reads as an unused import in between, and a half-written function reads as a
syntax error. Reporting those would train the agent to undo correct work.
{files} — scoping lint to what the agent edited
In lint, {files} expands to every path edited this session, shell-quoted. Use it when
the repo has a pre-existing lint backlog: project-wide lint fails at the end of every
task over files the agent never opened, and an agent handed someone else's errors once
will discount the gate afterwards.
"lint": "npx eslint --no-warn-ignored {files}"
An empty list skips the command rather than running it bare; paths that no longer exist
are dropped, and so are paths outside the project — Claude Code writes to ~/.claude for
plans and memory, and a tool that discovers its config per file fails the whole run on
one such path. A command without the placeholder stays project-wide, which is the
stronger gate — prefer it when the backlog is zero.
Do not put {files} in typecheck. tsc --noEmit needs the whole program, and individual
paths break tsconfig resolution while appearing to pass. The hook runs what you wrote
and will not correct this for you.
The command must also accept trailing paths: `npm run lint {files}` does not work (npm
needs `-- `), and a script pinned to its own path, like `eslint .`, ignores what is
appended. Verify before relying on it.
Monorepos — several checks per key
lint and typecheck also take a list, for packages that check themselves with different
tools. Every entry runs and every failure is reported; never chain with && instead.
"typecheck": [
{ "command": "npm run typecheck -w api", "when": "workspaces/api/**" },
{ "command": "npm run check -w admin", "when": "workspaces/admin/**" }
when is a glob relative to the project root. The check runs only if a path edited this
session matches it, and {files} in that check gets only the matching paths — so a
linter configured for one package is never handed files outside it. An entry without
when, or a bare string, runs whenever the gate does. format stays a single command.
test — watched, not run
Every other key is a command the gate runs at Stop. A test suite is the one that
cannot afford that: running it per turn costs minutes while the agent waits. So
`test.watch` names a watcher the gate starts in the background on the first edit of
the session, and at Stop the gate reads the verdict that watcher already produced.
"test": { "watch": "npx vitest --watch --reporter=json --outputFile={status}" }
{status} is required. The gate owns that path and reads JSON from it, expecting a
boolean `success` field (numFailedTests and numTotalTests are used for the message if
present). A watch command without the placeholder is dropped, because there would be
nothing to read — and a gate that cannot see a verdict is worse than no gate.
Freshness is the report file's mtime, not any timestamp inside it. Vitest's JSON
reporter rewrites `success` on every re-run but leaves `startTime` at the first run
for the life of the watch process, so a gate trusting that field would call every
verdict stale forever.
A report that is missing, older than the last edit, or unreadable blocks the turn and
says which. 'I could not tell whether the tests pass' is not permission to finish.
The watcher is stopped on SessionEnd.
Node's built-in test runner
node --test ships no reporter that carries a machine-readable verdict, so lint-gate
provides one. Point the runner at it and tell it where to write:
"test": { "watch": "LINT_GATE_STATUS={status} node --test --watch --test-reporter=${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/reporters/node-test-json.mjs" }
The path comes through the environment rather than --test-reporter-destination.
A reporter is an async generator over an event stream that never ends under --watch,
so one that emits after its loop emits nothing at all, and the report stays empty for
the life of the watch process.
